item.title: Pedestrian Trip Hazard: Raised EV Charging Cable Cover Across Public Pavement, 30th October
item.description:
I would like to report a potential pedestrian safety hazard caused by an electric vehicle charging cable running from a residential property across the public pavement to a parked vehicle. As shown in the attached photograph, the cable has been placed beneath a raised cable protector that extends across the width of the pavement. While I appreciate that the resident has taken steps to cover the cable, the protector itself creates a raised obstruction along the pedestrian walkway. I recently nearly tripped over the cable protector while walking along this pavement, particularly as it was dark and the obstruction was not immediately noticeable. I am concerned that this could pose a risk to other pedestrians, especially elderly residents, people with mobility difficulties, wheelchair users and parents with pushchairs. I understand that Bromley Council offers an EV charging cable gully scheme, which provides a recessed channel for charging cables to cross the pavement without creating a raised obstruction. I would therefore appreciate it if the Council could consider engaging with the resident and encouraging them to explore this scheme as a potentially safer, longer-term alternative. I would be grateful if the Council could: Assess the potential pedestrian safety risk associated with the raised cable protector. Consider whether any immediate measures are necessary to reduce the risk of trips and falls. Engage with the resident, where appropriate, to explore safer alternatives, including the Council's EV charging cable gully scheme. Thank you.
